claims.claim: Digital Realty sits on the AI/cloud infrastructure bottleneck through powered data-center capacity, connectivity and interconnection; Q2 backlog and new hyperscale leases show customers reserving scarce future capacity, while land acquisitions explicitly target multi-gigawatt utility power.
The successor bottleneck is power delivery and capital deployment: signed demand does not become usable compute infrastructure until utility power, construction and lease commencement occur.

causalEdges.mechanism: higher compute density and deployment requirements
leased compute hosting and network connectivity

risks.risk: Power availability and construction timing can delay conversion of signed backlog into revenue-bearing capacity.

unknowns.unknown: Incremental utility interconnection schedules by campus are not disclosed at sufficient granularity here.

claims.claim: Record backlog is not current revenue: Q2 new leases had a nine-month weighted-average commencement lag, so backlog can overstate near-term execution if read without timing.

Growth is capital intensive and partly equity financed: DLR had about $18.6B debt at Q2 end and sold about 13.5M shares year-to-date for roughly $2.5B, while also issuing shares in the Northern Virginia acquisition.
Headline Q2 FFO included material promote income and insurance recovery; Core FFO excluding net promote is the cleaner recurring execution reference.

risks.risk: Equity issuance and large development/acquisition commitments can dilute per-share participation if incremental returns disappoint.
Backlog conversion depends on power, construction and customer commencement rather than signature alone.

unknowns.unknown: Customer concentration within the largest new hyperscale leases is not resolved by the available release.
